properties.reasoning: No demonstrable alternative path to the plant's state within the declared zone (the agent container), the observation interval of the boundary run and the attempted classes. Topology: the plant runs in its own container with a write token only the API carries and a read token only the verifier carries; deploy/ot-pilot/credential_topology.yaml declares every secret the compose file hands out, its holders, its readers and the network membership, and scripts/check_ot_pilot_topology.py fails on each drift and on any unreachable credential the agent service carries. The agent service carries only OT_TOKEN_AGENT, and agent-net, which is internal, holds the agent and the API and nothing else; the live network membership read while the suite ran matched the register. Bypass: 53 attempts in the five minimum classes and two more (forged effect receipt, direct access to the authority store) were made from inside the agent container. No attempt changed the plant's state: in the run's interval the plant applied only the two governed control writes and refused no request, and every answer the agent saw was a refusal or a failure to connect or resolve. The agent's process table, environment and filesystem held no other credential. Coverage: the plant journals every request it answers (writes, reads and refusals; only the unauthenticated /health is not) with the credential it presented, and the state replayed from its journal equals the live state at the end of the interval; for the suite's interval every applied write names an executed REMORA dispatch and every executed write dispatch has exactly one applied write (two governed positive controls). A detector-sensitivity control in its own interval, a direct write with the executor's token from inside the API container, was reported as an unattributed write, so the reconciliation does see a bypass when one happens.
properties.caveat: A PASS here means no demonstrable alternative path within the declared zone, observation interval and attempted classes; it is not universal non-bypassability. The zone is the assessor's choice: drawn at the host, or at the API or verifier container, it does not hold, and the detector-sensitivity control shows code inside the API container reaching the plant (v0.1 section 12.3: an in-process runtime offers no custody; ot_registry refuses an in-process plant in production, and that refusal is tested). The topology check is static over the committed files and could miss an edge; the bypass suite needs only the running endpoint, the topology needs source access, so the procedure is asymmetric. Which component refused each attempt is not attributed. Docker and the kernel are trusted; one host, simulated plant, attempts written by the producer.

properties.reasoning: After every executed write the plant's state is read back by a verifier in another control domain, and REMORA computes the verdict itself. The verifier finds each executed dispatch through GET /v1/execution/dispatches, takes the plant journal's record of that dispatch, reads the object back with a read-only plant token at the revision that write produced (from the plant's history when a later write has moved it on) and signs a receipt with its own key; REMORA instantiates the postcondition from the signed ToolSpec (schema 5) and the approved arguments, accepts them only when they hash to the dispatched call, and derives the vantage independent from the key's registry record (another control domain, read-only scope). On an honest plant all 5 write tools verified, and in the battery 6 of 6 writes. On a plant with declared faults: a clamped valve is EFFECT_MISMATCH (field mismatch); a write acknowledged and never applied is EFFECT_MISMATCH (postcondition_effect_absent, from the unchanged revision); an object the verifier cannot read is EFFECT_UNOBSERVABLE and never VERIFIED; a write without a fault beside them verified. A receipt from an unregistered key, one posted with the agent's token, one with arguments other than the dispatched call's, and a replay after a settled verdict were refused, and the verdict did not move. A dispatch the plant has no record of is reported as an anomaly, not verified (in-process test).
properties.caveat: The verdict covers the declared delta only (scope declared_delta_only); fields a postcondition does not name are not compared. Independence rests on configuration REMORA reads (the executor's control domain, the key's domain and read-only scope), and on the plant reporting its state truthfully; the verifier and the plant are simulated and run on the same host. The fault set was written by the producer. The verdict itself names no writer; attribution on this pilot comes from the plant's revisions and journal (NEGATIVE_RESULTS section 85, narrowed here). Reads (read_sensor) declare no postcondition and are not verified.
